text_to_speech: Let's start to make a pizza with some ingredients.  We spread the sauce. We put on the ingredients and   the pizza goes into the oven. Oh wait! Did we miss  anything? Yes. We missed an essential ingredient.   The cheese. Now coming to the physics. Here we see  an elementary particle pizza. It has electrons,   quarks and other particles. but are there any that  we have missed? And where does gravity come into   play, which is like the cheese on this pizza.  Elementary particles are discovered in super   colliders by smashing big particles into one  another. But is there another way to know how   many particles are there? The answer is yes and it  involves gravity. A proposal is based on using the   two fundamental theories of physics, gravity  and quantum mechanics together. We prepare a   pencil particle in a Quantum superposition and  calculate the probabilities through beeping of   the detectors after it interacts gravitationally  with an extended Quantum system. We use these   probabilities to know how many of these stringy  things the particle interacted with in the first   place. These stringy things are progenitors of  elementary particles. Therefore we have designed   a new way, outside of super colliders, to know all  the ingredients of the elementary particle pizza.
